title: Apparent significant performance degradation in v1.5.9 vs v1.5.8
body:
Possibly related to: https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/issues/74#issuecomment-1677972732

SpiceDB (https://github.com/authzed/spicedb) makes use of the emulator for our Spanner datastore tests. We attempted to move to emulator v1.5.9 to enable testing of our use of changefeeds, but ran into immediate CI timeouts after ~10m.

After some investigation, it appears that v1.5.9 of the emulator is quite a bit slower than v1.5.8 for transactions containing somewhat large (~100s) of row insertions; I suspect this is due to the recent code necessary for book keeping for emulation of change feeds.

For reference, a test against v1.5.8 that executes a transaction with 256 rows inserted:

> PASS |     SpannerDatastore/TestSimple/256 (4.98s)

vs against v1.5.9:

> PASS |     SpannerDatastore/TestSimple/256 (35.51s)

I've found that the source of the slowdown is the first insertion transaction, which takes ~30s on average to add the 256 rows.

This is not blocking as we have moved back to v1.5.8 and can always increase the CI timeout, but we figured we'd mention it in case it becomes an issue for others

For reference, our Spanner-calling code can be found at https://github.com/authzed/spicedb/tree/main/internal/datastore/spanner

body:
Hi. If a table has a default value that needs to be converted to its type, inserting a record will cause emulator to terminate.

This is an example of TIMESTAMP type.

```shell
$ SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:9010 spanner-cli -p test-project -i test-instance -d test-database
Connected.
spanner> CREATE TABLE some_table (id INT64 NOT NULL, timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT ('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')) PRIMARY KEY (id);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

spanner> INSERT INTO some_table (id) VALUES (1);
ERROR: spanner: code = "DeadlineExceeded", desc = "context deadline exceeded"
spanner>  
```

```shell
$ docker run -ti --rm -p 9010:9010 gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.5.4
WARNING: proto: file "google/rpc/status.proto" is already registered
        previously from: "google.golang.org/genproto/googleapis/rpc/status"
        currently from:  "unknown"
See https://protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq#namespace-conflict

WARNING: proto: file "google/rpc/status.proto" has a name conflict over google.rpc.Status
        previously from: "google.golang.org/genproto/googleapis/rpc/status"
        currently from:  "unknown"
See https://protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq#namespace-conflict

WARNING: proto: message google.rpc.Status is already registered
        previously from: "google.golang.org/genproto/googleapis/rpc/status"
        currently from:  "unknown"
See https://protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq#namespace-conflict

2023/05/18 01:05:01 gateway.go:140: Cloud Spanner emulator running.
2023/05/18 01:05:01 gateway.go:141: REST server listening at 0.0.0.0:9020
2023/05/18 01:05:01 gateway.go:142: gRPC server listening at 0.0.0.0:9010
2023-05-18 01:05:38  FATAL  value.h : 605 : Check failed: ::absl::OkStatus() == ::zetasql::status_internal::AsStatus((value)) (OK vs. INTERNAL: ZETASQL_RET_CHECK failure (external/com_google_zetasql/zetasql/public/value.cc:249) field_type->Equals(value_type) 
Field type: TIMESTAMP
vs
Value type: STRING) 
2023/05/18 01:05:38 gateway.go:107: Shutting down gateway server since grpc server is terminated.
```

With Cloud Spanner, this works.

```shell
$ spanner-cli -p spanner-test-387100 -i test-instance -d test-database
Connected.
spanner> CREATE TABLE some_table (id INT64 NOT NULL, timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT ('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')) PRIMARY KEY (id);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (12.47 sec)

spanner> INSERT INTO some_table (id) VALUES (1);
Query OK, 1 rows affected (2.18 sec)

```
spanner> CREATE TABLE date_table (id INT64 NOT NULL, col_date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT ("1970-01-01")) PRIMARY KEY (id);

title: COLUMN_DEFAULT of INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returns incorrect value
body: The output of the COLUMN_DEFAULT column in Cloud Spanner Emulator's INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS may be missing when a function is used in the DEFAULT Value. Specifically, the brackets at the end of the function are missing. For example, create the following table on the Cloud Spanner Emulator v1.5.4. ``` CREATE TABLE test_table ( id INT64 NOT NULL, col_default_timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) ) PRIMARY KEY(id); ``` Then query INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS. ``` SELECT COLUMN_NAME, COLUMN_DEFAULT FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME="test_table"; ``` Expected output: ``` +-----------------------+---------------------+ | COLUMN_NAME | COLUMN_DEFAULT | +-----------------------+---------------------+ | id | NULL | | col_default_timestamp | CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() | +-----------------------+---------------------+ ``` Actual output: ``` +-----------------------+--------------------+ | COLUMN_NAME | COLUMN_DEFAULT | +-----------------------+--------------------+ | id | NULL | | col_default_timestamp | CURRENT_TIMESTAMP( | +-----------------------+--------------------+ ``` As mentioned above, the output should be `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()`, but it is output as `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(`. **The closing bracket `)` is missing**. As far as I have tested, this only occurs in Cloud Spanner Emulator v1.5.1 and later. v1.4.8 and v.1.5.0 print the expected output. https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1 The brackets in the value returned by `col->expression().value()` appear to have changed between v1.5.0 and v1.5.1, according to the revision history of `backend/schema/updater/schema_updater_tests/column_default_values.cc.` https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/v1.5.4/backend/query/information_schema_catalog.cc#L388-L389 I have not checked all the processes, but the process of trimming the brackets `()` is still left, so I suspect that only the `)` of `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()` was deleted here. This may seem like a minor issue, but if the results of `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` are used in the test of the application, the test will fail because the expected output is not obtained.

title: Usable as an external WORKSPACE
body:
**Note that I already have this working and am checking to see if y'all would like for me to contribute it back**

The Xoogler in me likes to have hermetic testing environments such that `bazel test //...` will run consistently across any environments where `bazel` is available and the source code is present. As such, I want all of my tests that are backed by Cloud Spanner to use a binary produced by `bazel` instead of having them depend on a binary installed somewhere on the system. 

This can be accomplished by including the `com_google_cloud_spanner_emulator` `WORKSPACE` as an external `WORKSPACE` in my project. Ideally, once all the dependencies are sorted out, running:
```
bazel run @com_google_cloud_spanner_emulator//binaries:gateway_main
```
should launch the emulator. However, I found some build issues that are only present when using the emulator as an external `WORKSPACE`. 

The three issues that I found and addressed are as follows:

1. The binary to populate the info schema columns metadata uses [hardcoded paths](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/16bdf843ac8ddabd06394c868d3b980d970a1bbc/backend/query/populate_info_schema_columns_metadata.cc#L51) to the metadata CSV files. I was able to address this issue by accessing the file paths via Runfiles.
2. The [rule to generate the DLLParser](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/16bdf843ac8ddabd06394c868d3b980d970a1bbc/backend/schema/parser/BUILD#L99) creates several `.cc` files that reference their headers via paths like: `#include "bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/external/com_google_cloud_spanner_emulator/backend/schema/parser/DDLParserTokenManager.h"`, but the generated `cc_libary` doesn't include the root build directory as a path to find headers. To address this issue, I added `-iquote .` to the `copts` list in the [generated cc_library rule](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/16bdf843ac8ddabd06394c868d3b980d970a1bbc/backend/common/javacc_parser.bzl#L114).
3. For some reason (that I still don't understand), [this patch](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/master/build/bazel/golang_protobuf.patch) doesn't get applied and doesn't cause an error. To address this issue, I added the following snippet to the [gateway_main](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/16bdf843ac8ddabd06394c868d3b980d970a1bbc/binaries/BUILD#L36) target, which has the benefit of only disabling the proto registration conflict errors for this specific binary (instead of for my whole project).
```
env = {
    "GOLANG_PROTOBUF_REGISTRATION_CONFLICT": "ignore",
},
```

As I mentioned above, I already have fixes for all of these issues and I'm currently applying them as a patch when I add `com_google_cloud_spanner_emulator` to my `WORKSPACE`. If you would like, I can send the changes as a PR to contribute them back to this repo. You can preview the changes [here](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...philstahlfeld:cloud-spanner-emulator:philstahlfeld-feat/ext-dep?expand=1).

title: DDL case sensitivity
body:
I've noticed that Spanner Emulator is more lenient with table name case than Spanner which has caused a few issues to slip past CI.

For example, imagine Spanner contains a table named `Account`. The statement:
```sql
ALTER TABLE ACCOUNT ADD COLUMN Test BOOL
```
runs successfully in the emulator and adds the column to the `Account` table. However, running the statement against Spanner fails with the error `Table ACCOUNT not found`.

Per the [docs](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#naming_conventions), 
> When referring to other schema objects in a DDL statement (for example, a column name for a primary key, or table and column names in an index), make sure to use the original case for the name of each entity.

so the emulator should error in this case.

title: Feature Request: Add statement hint to disable DDL statement in emulator.
body:
There are existing statement hints for the emulator, like:
```
@{spanner_emulator.disable_query_partitionability_check=true}
```

This feature request is to add a hint that will cause the emulator to skip a statement completely. E.g.:

```
@{spanner_emulator.skip_query=true}
```

This can be useful for a number of reasons, including:

- A statement is not required in testing.
- There is a lag between features being added to cloud Spanner and being added in the emulator. This means SQL scripts can't be used in the emulator despite them being valid. Emulator users need to create separate scripts and workarounds to handle it, which would be simplified by supporting a statement hint like this.

title: Precision of TIMESTAMP type is different
body:
On cloud-spanner-emulator, the following SQL will get the error `spanner: code = "OutOfRange", desc = "Invalid timestamp: '2022-03-31T23:59:59.999999999Z'"`

```sql
SELECT TIMESTAMP('2022-03-31T23:59:59.999999999Z');
```

However, Cloud Spanner does not return any error.

Also the emulator accept nanoseconds level value as TIMESTAMP type, but `MAX()` and `MIN()` returns microseconds's one.
For example, if `SomethingTable` has `CreatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL` column and value of `2022-03-31T14:59:59.999999999Z` was inserted.
The following SQL returns `2022-03-31T14:59:59.999999999Z`.

```sql
SELECT CreatedAt FROM SomethingTable
```

However, the following SQL returns `2022-03-31T14:59:59.999999Z`.

```sql
SELECT MAX(CreatedAt) FROM SomethingTable;
```

title: Arm64 Dockerfile
body:
m4 v1.4.18 has a bug that prevents it from compiling on arm64 architectures (for more information you can view https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/issues/29 and https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-m4/2021-03/msg00000.html).

This bug has been fixed in m4 v 1.4.19 but it has not been adapted into the upstream zetasql yet. The applied patch upgrades zetasqls m4 dependency to v1.4.19. This change also provide an arm64 docker container that can be used to build a working version of cloud-spanner-emulator.

This change also upgrades zetasql to the latest version to pull in some updates to the build tooling. While the previous version compiled, it had an older version of the build toolchain which caused the build to not be optimized. This resulted in a working binary but one that was ~30% slower than running the emlated amd64 docker container. Upgrading to the latest zetasql improved performance of the arm64 binary by ~155% based on local testing.

This is related to https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/issues/64 and https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/issues/29

title: Cloud Spanner Emulator version 1.4.1 (linux binary) no longer works on CentOS Stream 8
body:
### Summary
We are running CentOS Stream 8 in our environment.
Prior to the most recently released version, `1.4.1`, Spanner Emulator was running perfectly on CentOS 8.
Starting with `1.4.1` an attempt to run `gateway_main` on CentOS 8 results in an error:
```
/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.26' not found (required by /root/1.4.1/emulator_main)
2022/02/22 02:07:31 gateway.go:107: Shutting down gateway server since grpc server is terminated.
```

According to the documentation in this repository, it should work:
> Note that this binary is not fully static, but has been tested on Ubuntu 16.04/18.04, **CentOS 8, RHEL 8**, and Debian 9/10.

#### Possible root cause

It appears like the most recent version of binaries was built/linked on a machine with `GLIBCXX_3.4.26` support, with no hard linking to a specific GLIBCXX version. `GLIBCXX_3.4.26` symbols are supported as part of `libstdc++.so.6.0.26` binary which is part of the `GCC 9.1.0` ([source, GCC versioning documentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/abi.html)). CentOS 8/RHEL 8 is shipped with GCC 8 so binaries built for `GLIBCXX_3.4.26` are not going to work on CentOS 8/RHEL 8.

### Steps to reproduce
The easiest way to reproduce this issue would be to create a CentOS 8 docker container, download Spanner Emulator to it, and attempt to start it.

#### Dockerfile
I've defined the following `Dockerfile` which uses the official CentOS Stream 8 docker image and installs `wget` to download the emulator
```
FROM quay.io/centos/centos:stream

RUN yum install -y wget

ENTRYPOINT ["tail", "-f", "/dev/null"]
```

#### Preparing the test environment
To confirm that the issue is only present in the most recent version I'm going to run affected and unaffected versions on the same container.

To prepare the container I'm going to create two folders under `home` (one for `1.4.0` version and one for `1.4.1`), download two different versions of the emulator and unpack them to corresponding folders:
```
cd ~
mkdir 1.4.0
mkdir 1.4.1
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-spanner-emulator/releases/1.4.0/cloud-spanner-emulator_linux_amd64-1.4.0.tar.gz
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-spanner-emulator/releases/1.4.1/cloud-spanner-emulator_linux_amd64-1.4.1.tar.gz
tar zxvf cloud-spanner-emulator_linux_amd64-1.4.0.tar.gz -C ./1.4.0
tar zxvf cloud-spanner-emulator_linux_amd64-1.4.1.tar.gz -C ./1.4.1
```

#### Running emulator
First I'm going to run the `1.4.0` version to confirm that it works just fine:
```
./1.4.0/gateway_main --hostname 0.0.0.0
```
Output:
```
2022/02/22 02:07:07 gateway.go:140: Cloud Spanner emulator running.
2022/02/22 02:07:07 gateway.go:141: REST server listening at 0.0.0.0:9020
2022/02/22 02:07:07 gateway.go:142: gRPC server listening at 0.0.0.0:9010
```

Now I'm going to try and run the `1.4.1` version and see it fail:
```
./1.4.1/gateway_main --hostname 0.0.0.0
```
Output:
```
/root/1.4.1/emulator_main: /lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.26' not found (required by /root/1.4.1/emulator_main)
2022/02/22 02:07:31 gateway.go:107: Shutting down gateway server since grpc server is terminated.
```
Here is a screenshot of this reproduction example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/63533332/155052662-12806fa7-1b86-41a4-89c9-cb729e35c355.png)

title: Update README to point to version 1.3.0
Attempting to create a table that includes a `CHECK` constraint returns grpc `UNIMPLEMENTED`
body:
Google Cloud Spanner supports [a `CHECK` constraint](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/check-constraint/how-to), which allows the developer to add a constraint to a table that specifies some boolean condition that each row must satisfy. 

Suppose that I create a new table called `Foo` that has two nullable columns, and the expectation is that one of those columns will be non-null at any given time. I could create this table with the following SQL:
```
CREATE TABLE Foo (
    fooId STRING(255) NOT NULL,
    someId STRING(255),
    someOtherId STRING(255),
    CONSTRAINT someId_or_someOtherId_specified CHECK (someId IS NOT NULL OR someOtherId IS NOT NULL)
) PRIMARY KEY (
    fooId
)
```

In this case, the `someId_or_someOtherId` constraint will be evaluated whenever a row is inserted or updated in the `Foo` table. The operation will fail if the constraint evaluates to `FALSE`.

Problem is, the emulator does not support check constraints (this limitation [is documented in the emulator readme](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/master/README.md)) but rather than silently ignoring the constraint when data is inserted or updated, the emulator refuses to allow me to create the constraint in the first place. 

When I try to run a Flyway migration against the emulator that creates a table with a `CHECK` constraint, I get an error that looks like this:
```
Execution failed for task ':flyway:flywayMigrate'.
  Error occurred while executing flywayMigrate
  Migration failed !
  Migration failed !
  com.google.cloud.spanner.SpannerException: UNIMPLEMENTED: io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: UNIMPLEMENTED: Check Constraint is not implemented.
  UNIMPLEMENTED: io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: UNIMPLEMENTED: Check Constraint is not implemented.
  UNIMPLEMENTED: Check Constraint is not implemented.
```

Because my project uses this emulator for local development, I can't make use `CHECK` constraints in my schema, because doing so fails locally, even though these constraints **are fully supported by real Spanner**. 

This behaviour is not consistent with the behaviour that I see when making use of other Spanner functionality that the emulator does not support. As an example, I can create secondary indexes in my schema, even though [the emulator readme](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/master/README.md) says that they are not supported.

Is it possible for the emulator to silently ignore `CHECK` constraints in the same way that it ignores secondary indexes? This would allow me to include them in my schema, even though they are not evaluated when running test code against the emulator.

title: Emulator does not infer DATE & TIMESTAMP type for null values
body:
Originally raised in https://github.com/googleapis/python-spanner-django/issues/566, Spanner will infer the type of a null value if it is not provided but the emulator will throw an error for the same request. This has become an issue for Python ORMs as the suggestion to add this type inference logic to the DBAPI adapter is complicated and requires many changes.

Adding type inference for null values to the emulator to match the production behaviour would resolve the problem and allow us to confidently test against the emulator again.

title: Deleting a session with an active read/write transaction leaves the emulator in an invalid state
body:
If you execute the following steps:
1. Create a session with name `session-1`
2. Start a read/write transaction on `session-1`
3. Execute at least one statement on the read/write transaction on `session-1`
4. Delete `session-1` while the transaction is still active
5. Trying to commit/rollback the transaction on `session-1` will fail with a `Transaction not found` error.
6. Trying to begin a new read/write transaction will fail with the error that the emulator only supports one simultaneous transaction.

The above steps will therefore leave the emulator in an invalid state, as it is impossible to end the non-existing transaction, and also impossible to start a new one.

title: `ListDatabaseOperations` returns gRPC `Unimplemented ` status code
body:
From what I can tell, [the operation is implemented](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/a10bf75fefc5b47e75182df1acad73a0db5c7040/tests/conformance/cases/operations.cc#L105-L123), but when using the `ListDatabaseOperations`, the response is a gRPC `Unimplemented` code.

This was observed using [this method](https://googleapis.dev/java/google-cloud-spanner/latest/index.html) on the official Java client and confirmed with hitting the REST and gRPC APIs directly as shown here.

## To reproduce

### Start the emulator

```
docker run --rm -p 9020:9020 -p 9010:9010 gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.2.0
```

### Using the REST API

```
curl -I -XPOST  http://localhost:9020/v1/projects/test-project/instances/test-instance/databaseOperations
```

Response is:
```
HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2021 22:19:50 GMT
Content-Length: 19
```


### Using the gRPC API directly

1. Get the proto files for `grpcurl`

```
git clone https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis.git
```

2. invoke the gRPC method

```
grpcurl -import-path googleapis \
-proto googleapis/google/spanner/admin/database/v1/spanner_database_admin.proto \
-plaintext \
-d '{"parent":"projects/test-project/instances/test-instance"}' \
localhost:9010 \
google.spanner.admin.database.v1.DatabaseAdmin/ListDatabaseOperations
```

Response is:
```
ERROR:
  Code: Unimplemented
  Message:
```

title: ALTER TABLE ADD [COLUMN] statement requires COLUMN keyword
body:
The following DDL statement is accepted by Cloud Spanner and rejected by the emulator:

```sql
ALTER TABLE Singers ADD FullName STRING(500)
```

The emulator returns the following error for the above statement: `INVALID_ARGUMENT: Error parsing Spanner DDL statement: ALTER TABLE Singers ADD FullName STRING(500) : Syntax error on line 1, column 25: Expecting 'CHECK' but found 'FullName' [Failed SQL: (3) ALTER TABLE Singers ADD FullName STRING(500)]`

The emulator requires the statement to include the `COLUMN` keyword, although it according to the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/data-definition-language#alter_table) should be optional.

The following statement is successful on both the emulator and Cloud Spanner:

```sql
ALTER TABLE Singers ADD COLUMN FullName STRING(500)
```

title: default ordering of rows is different from live product

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

body:
Emulator and live product do not apply the same default sorting of records (when no `ORDER BY` is specified, or when multiple rows have the same value for the `ORDER BY` clause).

Here is how to replicate:

```
gcloud spanner instances create test-order \
  --config=emulator-config \
  --description="Test Instance" \
  --nodes=1

gcloud spanner databases create test \
 --instance=test-order \
 --ddl="CREATE TABLE test (a INT64, b INT64, c INT64,) PRIMARY KEY (a, b)"

gcloud spanner databases execute-sql test \
 --instance=test-order \
 --sql="INSERT test(a, b, c) VALUES (2, 1, 3), (2, 2, 3), (1, 2, 4)"

gcloud spanner databases execute-sql test \
 --instance=test-order \
 --sql="SELECT * FROM test"
```

Emulator returs:
```
a  b  c
2  1  3
1  2  4
2  2  3
```

Live returns:
```
a  b  c
1  2  4
2  1  3
2  2  3
```

-----

Now order by `a`:

```
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql test \
 --instance=test-order \
 --sql="SELECT * FROM test ORDER BY a ASC"
```


Emulator returs:
```
a  b  c
1  2  4
2  2  3
2  1  3
```

Live returns:
```
a  b  c
1  2  4
2  1  3
2  2  3
```

title: Emulator Performance / Paralleism
body:
Hi there,

Thanks for creating the Spanner Emulator. This tool has been instrumental in improving the reliability of the code we write with Spanner.

However, as we have added tests which depend on the emulator, often doing small (less than 10 rows), self contained things, we've noticed that the performance of our overall test suite has degraded significantly. After some analysis, we believe we're being heavily limited by the emulator, with simple operations (2 three row inserts) taking 30s+

We completely understand the note in the readme explaining that the Emulator's performance is not comparable to that of Cloud Spanner, but we're finding that as-is, it's a bit more limiting than we had hoped.

We're working in Go, with tests written to set up new DBs as described [in the recommended test setup](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator#what-is-the-recommended-test-setup) section. We're careful to not create databases we aren't using. We clean up the DBs as tests complete using Go's `t.Cleanup()` and the AdminClient's `DropDatabase` operation. (We have enough tests using the emulator that we can't skip this cleanup step, or we get errors about too many databases).

To help frame what we're seeing, I've run our test suite at multiple parallelism levels, both with build and test parallelism tuned to different levels, as well as disabled entirely.

```
go test -p 2 ./...  171.80s user 33.24s system 106% cpu 3:11.84 total
go test -p 4 ./...  183.28s user 37.14s system 150% cpu 2:26.87 total
go test -p 8 ./...  205.39s user 44.78s system 178% cpu 2:20.04 total
go test -p 16 ./...  218.39s user 51.40s system 197% cpu 2:16.49 total
```

- By default, that `-p` value is set to GOMAXPROCS, which is the number of core-threads on your machine. So for the computer I am on, the default is `-p 16` for me (8 cores, 2 threads per core).
- In each of the test observations, the emulator was the dominant CPU usage on my mac, with `go test` mostly idle, as reported by `htop`.
- **The emulator appears to max out at about 100% of one core, even though I've dedicated 4 cores to the docker-for-mac VM that it's running in.**
- `-p 4` appears to be the last point at which there's a real gain in wall-clock time, demonstrating to me a clear concurrency bottleneck.
- I cleared the go test cache before each of those runs.
- The Emulator has this in it's documentation: "The emulator only allows one read-write transaction or schema change at a time. Any concurrent transaction will be aborted.". I'm not really sure what this means (ie, process wide, or per-DB?), but I have a hunch it's not good for running concurrent tests.
- Without the Spanner Emulator tests enabled (ie, by calling `t.SkipNow()`), our test suite takes about 30s.

Given those observations, what are some strategies we could take for getting our test time down? Are there performance or concurrency improvements for the emulator coming on the horizon?

Thank you!
